metadata.title: Thresholds for $(n,q,2)$-Steiner Systems via Refined Absorption
metadata.authors: Michelle Delcourt, Tom Kelly, Luke Postle

nodes.name: Steiner system / design / BIBD
nodes.statement: An $(n,q,r)$-Steiner system is a set $S$ of $q$-subsets of an $n$-set $X$ such that every $r$-subset of $X$ belongs to exactly one element of $S$; an $(n,q,r,\lambda)$-design requires every $r$-subset to lie in exactly $\lambda$ elements.

nodes.name: Divisibility conditions for Steiner systems
nodes.statement: An $(n,q,r)$-Steiner system requires $\binom{q-i}{r-i} \mid \binom{n-i}{r-i}$ for all $i \in \{0,\dots,r-1\}$. For $r=2$: $q-1 \mid n-1$ and $\binom{q}{2} \mid \binom{n}{2}$.

nodes.name: Random $q$-uniform hypergraph and threshold
nodes.statement: $\mathcal{G}^{(q)}(n,p)$ is the random $n$-vertex $q$-uniform hypergraph in which each $q$-set is independently included with probability $p$. A function $p^*(n)$ is a $\textit{threshold}$ for an increasing property $\mathcal{P}$ if $\Prob{\mathcal{G}^{(q)}(n_i,p)\in\mathcal{P}}\to 0$ for $p=o(p^*)$ and $\to 1$ for $p=\omega(p^*)$.

nodes.name: $F$-packing, $F$-decomposition, $K_q$-divisibility
nodes.statement: An $F$-packing of $G$ is a collection $\mathcal{H}$ of pairwise edge-disjoint subgraphs of $G$ each isomorphic to $F$; an $F$-decomposition additionally covers every edge of $G$. $G$ is $K_q$-divisible if $q-1 \mid d(v)$ for all $v$ and $\binom{q}{2} \mid e(G)$.

nodes.name: $\sigma$-spread distribution on $K_q$-decompositions
nodes.statement: A probability distribution on $K_q$-decompositions $\mathcal{H}$ of a graph $G$ is $\sigma$-spread if $\Prob{\mathcal{S}\subseteq\mathcal{H}} \leq \sigma^{|\mathcal{S}|}$ for every $K_q$-packing $\mathcal{S}$ of $G$.

nodes.name: $K_q$-absorber
nodes.statement: For a $K_q$-divisible graph $L$, a graph $A$ is a $K_q$-absorber for $L$ if $V(L)\subseteq V(A)$ is independent in $A$ and both $A$ and $L\cup A$ admit $K_q$-decompositions.

nodes.name: $K_q$-omni-absorber
nodes.statement: A graph $A$ is a $K_q$-omni-absorber for $X$ with decomposition family $\mathcal{H}$ and decomposition function $\mathcal{Q}_A$ if $V(X)=V(A)$, $X$ and $A$ are edge-disjoint, every $H\in\mathcal{H}$ is a $K_q$ with $|E(H)\cap E(X)|\le 1$, and for every $K_q$-divisible $L\subseteq X$ there exists $\mathcal{Q}_A(L)\subseteq\mathcal{H}$ pairwise edge-disjoint with $\bigcup\mathcal{Q}_A(L)=L\cup A$.

nodes.name: $C$-refined omni-absorber
nodes.statement: A $K_q$-omni-absorber $A$ for $X$ with decomposition family $\mathcal{H}$ is $C$-refined if $|\{H\in\mathcal{H}:e\in E(H)\}| \le C$ for every edge $e\in X\cup A$.

nodes.name: Design hypergraph
nodes.statement: For a hypergraph $F$ and a hypergraph $G$, the $F$-design hypergraph $\mathrm{Design}(G,F)$ is the hypergraph $\Gamma$ with $V(\Gamma)=E(G)$ and $E(\Gamma)=\{S\subseteq E(G):S\cong F\}$.

nodes.name: Bipartite hypergraph and $A$-perfect matching
nodes.statement: A hypergraph $G=(A,B)$ is bipartite with parts $A$ and $B$ if $V(G)=A\cup B$ and every edge contains exactly one vertex from $A$. A matching is $A$-perfect if every vertex of $A$ is in an edge of the matching.

nodes.name: $K_q$-booster and rooted $K_q$-booster
nodes.statement: A $K_q$-booster is a graph $B$ with two disjoint $K_q$-decompositions $\mathcal{B}^{\circ}$ and $\mathcal{B}^{\filledcirc}$. A rooted $K_q$-booster $(B,\mathcal{B}^{\circ},\mathcal{B}^{\filledcirc},R)$ has $R\cong K_q$ edge-disjoint from $B$, $\mathcal{B}^{\filledcirc}$ a $K_q$-decomposition of $B$ (off-decomposition), and $\mathcal{B}^{\circ}$ a $K_q$-decomposition of $B\cup R$ with $R\notin\mathcal{B}^{\circ}$ (on-decomposition).

nodes.name: Rooted density and maximum rooted density
nodes.statement: For a $K_q$-packing $\mathcal{H}$ of $G$ and $R\subseteq V(G)$: $d(\mathcal{H},R) := |\mathcal{H}|/|\bigcup_{H\in\mathcal{H}}V(H)\setminus R|$, and $m(\mathcal{H},R) := \max_{\mathcal{H}'\subseteq\mathcal{H}}d(\mathcal{H}',R)$. The rooted density of a rooted booster $(B,\mathcal{B}^{\circ},\mathcal{B}^{\filledcirc},R)$ is $\max_{\mathcal{H}\in\{\mathcal{B}^{\circ},\mathcal{B}^{\filledcirc}\}} m(\mathcal{H},R)$.

nodes.name: Partial $K_k$ rooted at $R$
nodes.statement: A partial $K_k$ rooted at $R$ is a graph $T$ with $R\subseteq V(T)$, $|V(T)|=k$, and $E(T)=\binom{V(T)}{2}\setminus\binom{R}{2}$.

nodes.name: Park-Pham Theorem
nodes.statement: There is an absolute constant $K>0$ such that if there exists a $\sigma_n$-spread probability distribution on $K_q$-decompositions of $K_n$ and $p \geq K\sigma_n\log n$, then $\mathcal{G}^{(q)}(n,p)$ a.a.s. contains an $(n,q,2)$-Steiner system.
assumptions: Existence of a $\sigma_n$-spread distribution on $K_q$-decompositions of $K_n$

nodes.name: Refined Omni-Absorber Theorem (graph version)
nodes.statement: For every integer $q\ge 3$ there exists $C\ge 1$ such that: if $X$ is a spanning subgraph of $K_n$ with $\Delta(X) \le n/C$ and $\Delta := \max\{\Delta(X),\sqrt{n}\log n\}$, then there exists a $C$-refined $K_q$-omni-absorber $A\subseteq K_n$ for $X$ with $\Delta(A)\le C\cdot\Delta$.

nodes.name: Existence of $(n,q,2)$-Steiner systems in random hypergraph
nodes.statement: For every integer $q>2$, if $q-1\mid n-1$ and $\binom{q}{2}\mid\binom{n}{2}$ and $p\geq n^{-(q-6)/2}$, then a.a.s. $\mathcal{G}^{(q)}(n,p)$ contains an $(n,q,2)$-Steiner system.

nodes.name: Spread $K_q$-decomposition existence
nodes.statement: For every integer $q>2$, there exists $\beta>0$ such that for all sufficiently large $n$: if $K_n$ is $K_q$-divisible, then there exists an $(n^{-(q-6)/2-\beta})$-spread probability distribution on $K_q$-decompositions of $K_n$.
conclusions: There exists an $(n^{-(q-6)/2-\beta})$-spread distribution on $K_q$-decompositions of $K_n$ for some $\beta>0$

nodes.name: Spread Refined Omni-Absorber Theorem
nodes.statement: For every integer $q\ge 3$, for sufficiently large $n,C$ with $C\le\sqrt{n}/\log n$: if $X\subseteq G\cong K_n$ has $\Delta(X)\le n/C$, then there exists a distribution over $K_q$-omni-absorbers $A\subseteq G$ for $X$ with $\Delta(A)\le C\cdot\max\{\Delta(X),\sqrt{n}\log n\}$ and $\Prob{\bigcup_{L\subseteq X}\{\mathcal{S}\subseteq\mathcal{Q}_A(L)\}}\le (1/(C^{1/4}n^{(q-6)/2}))^{|\mathcal{S}|}$ for every $K_q$-packing $\mathcal{S}$.
assumptions: $X$ spanning subgraph of $G\cong K_n$ with $\Delta(X)\le n/C$
conclusions: There exists a distribution on $K_q$-omni-absorbers $A$ for $X$ with $\Delta(A)\le C\Delta$

nodes.name: Nibble with reserves
nodes.statement: For all $r\ge 2$ and $\beta\in(0,1)$, there exist $D_\beta$ and $\alpha>0$ such that for $D\ge D_\beta$: if $G$ is an $r$-uniform hypergraph with codegrees at most $D^{1-\beta}$, edge-disjoint union of $G_1$ and bipartite $G_2=(A,B)$ with appropriate degree conditions on $A$, $B$, $G_1$, $G_2$, then there exists an $A$-perfect matching of $G$.
assumptions: $G_2=(A,B)$ bipartite; vertices of $B$ have degree $\le D$ in $G_2$
Vertices of $A$ have degree $\ge D^{1-\alpha}$ in $G_2$ and $\ge D(1-D^{-\beta})$ in $G_1$

nodes.name: Spread Nibble with Reserves
nodes.statement: For all $r,\gamma,\beta>0$ and sufficiently large $D$, sufficiently small $\alpha>0$: under the hypotheses of nibble with reserves, there exists a probability distribution on $A$-perfect matchings $M$ of $G$ such that $\Prob{S\subseteq M}\le (1/D^{1-\gamma})^{|S|}$ for every $S\subseteq E(G)$.
conclusions: There exists a $D^{-(1-\gamma)}$-spread distribution on $A$-perfect matchings $M$ of $G$

nodes.name: Reservoir Lemma
nodes.statement: For every integer $q\ge 3$, there exists $\varepsilon>0$ such that for sufficiently large $n$: if $G$ is $n$-vertex with $\delta(G)\ge(1-\varepsilon)n$ and $1/n^\varepsilon\le p\le 1$, then there exists $X\subseteq G$ with $\Delta(X)\le 2pn$ such that for all $e\in E(G)\setminus E(X)$, there are at least $\varepsilon p^{\binom{q}{2}-1}n^{q-2}$ $K_q$'s in $X\cup\{e\}$ containing $e$.
conclusions: There exists $X\subseteq G$ with $\Delta(X)\le 2pn$ and the stated $K_q$-extension property

nodes.name: Boosting / Regularity-Boost Lemma
nodes.statement: For every integer $q\ge 3$, there exists $\varepsilon>0$ such that for sufficiently large $n$: if $J$ is an $n$-vertex graph with $\delta(J)\ge(1-\varepsilon)n$, then there exists a subhypergraph $\mathcal{D}$ of $\mathrm{Design}(J,K_q)$ with $d_{\mathcal{D}}(v) = (1/2 \pm n^{-(q-2)/3})\binom{n-2}{q-2}$ for all $v$.

nodes.name: Conditional Lovasz Local Lemma
nodes.statement: Let $\{X_i\}_{i\in I}$ be independent random variables and $\{\mathcal{E}_j\}_{j\in J}$ events with $\mathcal{E}_j$ depending on $S_j\subseteq I$. Let $\Gamma$ be a graph on $J$ with $S_j\cap S_{j'}=\emptyset$ for non-adjacent $j,j'$. If $\Prob{\mathcal{E}_j}\le p$ for all $j$ and $4p\Delta(\Gamma)\le 1$, then $\ProbCond{\mathcal{E}}{\bigcap_j\overline{\mathcal{E}_j}}\le\Prob{\mathcal{E}}\exp(6pN)$ where $N$ is the number of $\mathcal{E}_j$ with $S_j\cap S\neq\emptyset$.
assumptions: $\{X_i\}$ independent; $\{\mathcal{E}_j\}$ events with proper dependency graph $\Gamma$

nodes.name: Sparse boosters exist
nodes.statement: For every integer $q>2$, there exists a rooted $K_q$-booster with rooted density at most $2/(q-2)$.
conclusions: There exists a rooted $K_q$-booster $(B,\mathcal{B}^{\circ},\mathcal{B}^{\filledcirc},R)$ with rooted density $\le 2/(q-2)$

nodes.name: Vertex-Spread Clique Embedding
nodes.statement: For all integers $q\ge 3$, $b\ge 1$, sufficiently small $\varepsilon$ and large $C$: if $G$ has $\delta(G)\ge(1-\varepsilon)n$ and $\mathcal{H}$ is a $q$-uniform hypergraph on $V(G)$ with $\Delta_1(\mathcal{H})\le n/C$, then there exists a distribution on pairwise edge-disjoint $T_e\subseteq G$, each a partial $K_{q+b}$ rooted at $V(e)$, with $\Delta(\bigcup T_e)\le C\Delta_1(\mathcal{H})$ and $\Prob{S_e\subseteq V(T_e)\setminus V(e)\,\forall e}\le ((3b)^b/n)^{\sum|S_e|}$.
conclusions: Existence of distribution on edge-disjoint partial $K_{q+b}$'s rooted at $V(e)$
Maximum-degree bound and vertex-spreadness bound as stated

nodes.name: Booster with one special clique
nodes.statement: For every integer $q>2$, there exists a $K_q$-booster $B$ with disjoint decompositions $\mathcal{B}_1$, $\mathcal{B}_2$ and $S_i\in\mathcal{B}_i$ with $|V(S_1)\cap V(S_2)|=q-1$ such that $m(\mathcal{B}_1\setminus\{S_1\},V(S_1))\le 2/(q-2)$ and $m(\mathcal{B}_2\setminus\{S_2\},V(S_1)\cup V(S_2))\le 2/(q-2)$.
conclusions: Existence of a $K_q$-booster with two disjoint $K_q$-decompositions and special cliques $S_1, S_2$ as described
Rooted density bounds excluding the special clique are $\le 2/(q-2)$

nodes.name: KKKMO Conjecture (Kang-Kelly-Kuhn-Methuku-Osthus)
nodes.statement: For every $q,r\in\mathbb{N}$ with $q>r$: if $\binom{q-i}{r-i}\mid\binom{n-i}{r-i}$ for all $i$ and $p=\omega(n^{-q+r}\log n)$, then a.a.s. $\mathcal{G}^{(q)}(n,p)$ contains an $(n,q,r)$-Steiner system.

nodes.name: Proof of Spread Omni-Absorber Theorem (Theorem 4.1)
nodes.section: 4.3 Proof of the Spread Omni-Absorber Theorem
nodes.statement: Combine Theorem 2.3, Lemma 4.4 (sparse rooted booster), and Lemma 4.5 (vertex-spread clique embedding): start from a $C'$-refined omni-absorber $A'$, embed pairwise edge-disjoint partial $K_{q+b}$'s containing private boosters for each $H\in\mathcal{H}_{A'}$, replace each $H$ with the chosen booster's two decompositions, and bound the spread by union bound over partitions of any packing $\mathcal{S}$.

nodes.name: Proof of Sparse Boosters Exist (Lemma 4.4)
nodes.section: 5 Construction of Spread Boosters (proof of Lemma 4.4)
nodes.statement: Take a booster $B$ minimizing $|V(S_1)\cap V(S_2)|$ subject to the conclusions of Lemma 5.1. If $|V(S_1)\cap V(S_2)|=0$, the rooted booster $(B-E(S_1),\mathcal{B}_2,\mathcal{B}_1\setminus\{S_1\},S_1)$ has rooted density $\le 2/(q-2)$; otherwise glue another copy of the construction along $S_2$ to strictly decrease the intersection, contradicting minimality.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 5.1 (Booster with one special clique)
nodes.section: 5 Construction of Spread Boosters (proof of Lemma 5.1)
nodes.statement: Construct $B$ with $V(B)=\{v_1,v_2\}\cup[q-1]\times[q-1]$, taking horizontal/vertical $K_{q-1}$ rows of the $K_{q-1}\square K_{q-1}$ Cartesian product extended to $K_q$'s using $v_1,v_2$. Two disjoint $K_q$-decompositions $\mathcal{B}_1,\mathcal{B}_2$ arise; rooted-density bounds follow by counting horizontal vs vertical cliques.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 4.5 (Vertex-Spread Clique Embedding)
nodes.statement: Sample each $T_e\in\mathcal{X}_e$ and index $i_e\in[D]$ uniformly and independently; define bad events $J_1$ (degree exceeds $C\Delta_1(\mathcal{H})$) and $J_2$ (edge-overlap between distinct $T_e$'s) and apply the conditional Lovasz Local Lemma to obtain the desired distribution and spreadness bound.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 5.2 (Spread Nibble)
nodes.section: 5 Spread Nibble with Reserves (proof of Theorem 5.1)
nodes.statement: Sparsify by including each edge of $G_1, G_2$ independently with probability $D^{\gamma/2-1}$, control codegrees and degrees via Chernoff and the Lovasz Local Lemma, apply Theorem 3.7 (nibble with reserves) on the surviving hypergraph, and bound the conditional spread of $S\subseteq M$ by $(2D^{\gamma/2-1})^{|S|}\le D^{-(1-\gamma)|S|}$.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 1.3 (Spread $K_q$-decomposition)
nodes.statement: Let $C=n^{8\beta}$, $p=C^{-2}/2$. Apply Lemma 3.1 to get the reservoir $X$, Theorem 4.1 to get a spread random omni-absorber $A$, Lemma 3.3 (regularity boost) on $J_A=G-(X\cup A)$ to get $\mathcal{D}_1^A$, build the bipartite design $\mathcal{D}_2^A$, apply Theorem 5.1 to get a spread $E(J_A)$-perfect matching $M_A$, and combine with $\mathcal{Q}_A(L_{A,M_A})$. Bound the joint spread by summing over partitions $\mathcal{S}'\subseteq\mathcal{S}$ using the omni-absorber spread and the nibble spread.

nodes.name: Apply $C'$-refined omni-absorber black box
nodes.statement: Apply Theorem~\ref{thm:omni-absorber} to obtain a $C'$-refined omni-absorber $A'$ for $X$ with decomposition family $\mathcal{H}_{A'}$, decomposition function $\mathcal{Q}_{A'}$, and $\Delta(A')\le C'\Delta$ where $\Delta=\max\{\Delta(X),\sqrt{n}\log n\}$.

nodes.name: Choose sparse rooted booster template
nodes.statement: By Lemma~\ref{lem:sparse-boosters-exist}, fix a rooted $K_q$-booster $(\tilde B,\mathcal{B}^{\circ},\mathcal{B}^{\filledcirc},R)$ with rooted density $\le 2/(q-2)$ and let $b:=|V(\tilde B)\setminus V(R)|$.

nodes.name: Embed pairwise-disjoint partial $K_{q+b}$'s by Lemma 4.5
nodes.statement: Apply Lemma~\ref{lemma:spread-clique-embedding} to $G-(X\cup A')$ and $\mathcal{H}_{A'}$ to obtain pairwise edge-disjoint partial $K_{q+b}$'s $T_H$ rooted at $V(H)$ with $\Delta(T)\le C\Delta/2$ satisfying the vertex-spreadness bound (4.2).

nodes.name: Replace each $H$ with a private booster
nodes.statement: For each $H\in\mathcal{H}_{A'}$ choose a rooted booster $(B_H,\mathcal{B}_H^{\circ},\mathcal{B}_H^{\filledcirc},H)\subseteq T_H$ isomorphic to $\tilde B$. Let $A := A'\cup\bigcup_H B_H$, $\mathcal{H}_A := \bigcup_H(\mathcal{B}_H^{\circ}\cup\mathcal{B}_H^{\filledcirc})$, and define $\mathcal{Q}_A(L)$ from $\mathcal{Q}_{A'}(L)$ in the natural way.

nodes.name: Bound number of partitions of $\mathcal{S}$
nodes.statement: Let $\mathcal{P}$ index $((\mathcal{S}_H,*_H):H\in\mathcal{H}_{A'})$ where $(\mathcal{S}_H)$ is a partition of $\mathcal{S}$ and $*_H\in\{\circ,\filledcirc\}$. Then $|\mathcal{P}|\le(n^2/C^{3/4})^{|\mathcal{S}|}$.

nodes.name: Bound probability per partition via rooted density
nodes.statement: Use rooted density $\le 2/(q-2)$ to get $|\bigcup_S V(S)\setminus V(H)|\ge(q-2)|\mathcal{S}'|/2$, then by (4.2): $\Prob{\mathcal{S}_H\subseteq\mathcal{B}_H^{*_H}\,\forall H}\le(\sqrt{C}/n^{(q-2)/2})^{|\mathcal{S}|}$.

nodes.name: Combine via union bound
nodes.statement: Multiply the partition count and per-partition probability to get $\Prob{\bigcup_L\{\mathcal{S}\subseteq\mathcal{Q}_A(L)\}}\le(C^{-1/4}n^{-(q-6)/2})^{|\mathcal{S}|}$ as desired.

nodes.name: Choose minimal-intersection booster from Lemma 5.1
nodes.statement: Among $K_q$-boosters $B$ with disjoint decompositions $\mathcal{B}_1,\mathcal{B}_2$ and special cliques $S_1,S_2$ satisfying (5.1.1)-(5.1.2), pick one with $|V(S_1)\cap V(S_2)|$ minimum. Such a booster exists by Lemma~\ref{lem:spread-booster-w-special-clique}.

nodes.name: Base case: disjoint special cliques
nodes.statement: If $|V(S_1)\cap V(S_2)|=0$, then $(B-E(S_1),\mathcal{B}_2,\mathcal{B}_1\setminus\{S_1\},S_1)$ is a rooted booster; verify rooted density bound by case analysis on whether $S_2\in\mathcal{H}$ for any $\mathcal{H}\subseteq\mathcal{B}_2$.

nodes.name: Inductive step: glue another booster along $S_2$
nodes.statement: If $V(S_1)\cap V(S_2)\ne\emptyset$, take a fresh booster $B'$ from Lemma~\ref{lem:spread-booster-w-special-clique} with $S_1' = S_2$ and $V(S_1')\setminus V(S_2')\subseteq V(S_1)\cap V(S_2)$. Define $B''=B\cup B'$, $\mathcal{B}_1''$, $\mathcal{B}_2''$ as the merged decompositions.

nodes.name: Verify density bounds on $B''$ contradict minimality
nodes.statement: Show $m(\mathcal{B}_1'',V(S_1))\le 2/(q-2)$ and $m(\mathcal{B}_2''\setminus\{S_2'\},V(S_1)\cup V(S_2'))\le 2/(q-2)$ by partitioning $\mathcal{H}\subseteq\mathcal{B}_1''$ into $\mathcal{H}_1\subseteq\mathcal{B}_1$ and $\mathcal{H}_2\subseteq\mathcal{B}_1'\setminus\{S_1'\}$ and applying (5.1.1) and (5.1.1'). Since $|V(S_1)\cap V(S_2')|<|V(S_1)\cap V(S_2)|$, this contradicts minimality unless the base case applies.

nodes.name: Construct base graph $B$
nodes.statement: Let $V(B)=\{v_1,v_2\}\cup[q-1]\times[q-1]$, with $v_1,v_2$ adjacent to every $(i,j)$, and $(i,j)\sim(i',j')$ iff $i=i'$ or $j=j'$ (Cartesian product $K_{q-1}\square K_{q-1}$ plus two dominators).

nodes.name: Define horizontal and vertical $K_q$ cliques
nodes.statement: For each $i\in[q-1]$, $x\in\{1,2\}$, $Q^{\hoclique}_{i,x}=\{v_x\}\cup\{(i,j):j\in[q-1]\}$; for each $j$, $Q^{\vertclique}_{j,x}=\{v_x\}\cup\{(i,j):i\in[q-1]\}$.

nodes.name: Form two disjoint $K_q$-decompositions
nodes.statement: Set $\mathcal{B}_1:=\{B[Q^{\hoclique}_{i,1}]\}\cup\{B[Q^{\vertclique}_{j,2}]\}$ and $\mathcal{B}_2:=\{B[Q^{\hoclique}_{i,2}]\}\cup\{B[Q^{\vertclique}_{j,1}]\}$. These are disjoint $K_q$-decompositions of $B$.

nodes.name: Choose special cliques and verify intersection
nodes.statement: Let $S_1:=B[Q^{\hoclique}_{1,1}]$, $S_2:=B[Q^{\hoclique}_{1,2}]$. Then $S_i\in\mathcal{B}_i$ and $|V(S_1)\cap V(S_2)|=q-1$ (the row $i=1$).

nodes.name: Bound rooted density via horizontal/vertical split
nodes.statement: For any $\mathcal{H}\subseteq\mathcal{B}_1\setminus\{S_1\}$, split into horizontal $\mathcal{H}^{\hoclique}$ and vertical $\mathcal{H}^{\vertclique}$. Each contributes $(q-1)|\mathcal{H}^{\hoclique}|$ resp. $(q-2)|\mathcal{H}^{\vertclique}|$ vertices outside $V(S_1)$, so $d(\mathcal{H},V(S_1))\le|\mathcal{H}|/((q-2)\max\{|\mathcal{H}^{\hoclique}|,|\mathcal{H}^{\vertclique}|\})\le 2/(q-2)$. Same for $\mathcal{B}_2$.

nodes.name: Setup random embedding
nodes.statement: Set $\Delta:=\Delta_1(\mathcal{H})$, $D:=\lfloor C\Delta/(2(q+b))\rfloor$. For each $e\in\mathcal{H}$, let $\mathcal{X}_e$ be the set of partial $K_{q+b}$'s rooted at $V(e)$. Sample $T_e\in\mathcal{X}_e$ and $i_e\in[D]$ independently and uniformly. Use $|\mathcal{X}_e|\ge(n/(2b))^b$ and $|\{T\in\mathcal{X}_e:V(T)\supseteq S\}|\le n^{b-|S|}$.

nodes.name: Define bad events $J_1$ (degree blowup)
nodes.statement: $J_1$: tuples $(T_1,T_2,v,i)$ with $T_j\in\mathcal{X}_{e_j}$ distinct, $v\in(V(T_1)\setminus V(e_1))\cap(V(T_2)\setminus V(e_2))$, $i\in[D]$. Forbidding $J_1$ ensures $\Delta(T)\le C\Delta_1(\mathcal{H})$.

nodes.name: Define bad events $J_2$ (edge collisions)
nodes.statement: $J_2$: tuples $(T_1,T_2,f,i_1,i_2)$ with $T_j\in\mathcal{X}_{e_j}$ distinct, $f\in E(T_1)\cap E(T_2)$. Forbidding $J_2$ ensures the $T_e$'s are pairwise edge-disjoint.

nodes.name: Bound dependency degree of $\Gamma$
nodes.statement: Counting arguments using $|\mathcal{X}_e|$ bounds give every node of $\Gamma$ at most $6D^2(q+b)^2n^{2b}/C$ neighbours in $J_2$ and $12D^2(q+b)^2n^{2b}/C$ in $J_1$, so $\Delta(\Gamma)\le 18D^2(q+b)^2n^{2b}/C$.

nodes.name: Apply conditional Lovasz Local Lemma
nodes.statement: Apply Lemma~\ref{lem:conditionalLLL} with $p=(2b/n)^{2b}D^{-2}$. The conditional distribution on $\bigcap_j\overline{\mathcal{E}_j}$ yields edge-disjoint $T_e$'s of bounded degree.

nodes.name: Bound conditional spread of $S_e\subseteq V(T_e)\setminus V(e)$
nodes.statement: For $\mathcal{E}=\{S_e\subseteq V(T_e)\setminus V(e)\,\forall e\}$ with $|S_e|\le b$ and $S_e\cap V(e)=\emptyset$: $\Prob{\mathcal{E}}\le((2b)^b/n)^{\sum|S_e|}$ and conditional probability $\le((3b)^b/n)^{\sum|S_e|}$ via the LLL exponential factor.

nodes.name: Random sparsification of $G_1, G_2$
nodes.statement: Set $\gamma$ small w.r.t. $\beta$, $\alpha$ small w.r.t. $\gamma$. Include each $e\in E(G_i)$ in $G'_i$ independently with probability $D^{\gamma/2-1}$, take $G'\subseteq G'_1\cup G'_2$.

nodes.name: Define Chernoff bad events
nodes.statement: Define events $\mathcal{E}_{\{u,v\}}$ (codegree exceeds $\log^2 D$ in $G'$), $\mathcal{E}_b, \mathcal{E}_{(v,0)}$ (degrees in $G'_2,G'_1$ too high), $\mathcal{E}_{(a,1)}, \mathcal{E}_{(a,2)}$ (degrees of $a\in A$ too low).

nodes.name: Build dependency graph and bound probabilities
nodes.statement: Form $\Gamma$ on these events with $\Delta(\Gamma)\le 5r^2 D$. By Chernoff, $\Prob{\mathcal{E}_j}\le\exp(-\log^2 D)$ for every $j\in V(\Gamma)$.

nodes.name: Apply nibble-with-reserves on surviving hypergraph
nodes.statement: When $\bigcap_j\overline{\mathcal{E}_j}$ holds, apply Theorem~\ref{thm:NibbleReserves} with $G',G'_1,G'_2$ and parameters $D^{\gamma/2}+D^{\gamma/3}$, $1/4$, $3\alpha/\gamma$ to obtain an $A$-perfect matching $M\subseteq G'$.

nodes.name: Bound conditional spread via LLL
nodes.statement: For $S\subseteq E(G)$, $\mathcal{E}=\{S\subseteq E(G')\}$, by Lemma~\ref{lem:conditionalLLL}: $\ProbCond{\mathcal{E}}{\bigcap_j\overline{\mathcal{E}_j}}\le(2D^{\gamma/2-1})^{|S|}\le(D^{-(1-\gamma)})^{|S|}$. Since $S\subseteq M\Rightarrow S\subseteq E(G')$, the result follows.

nodes.name: Set parameters and produce reservoir $X$
nodes.statement: Take $G\cong K_n$, $C:=n^{8\beta}$, $p:=C^{-2}/2$. By Lemma~\ref{lem:reservoir} obtain $X\subseteq G$ with $\Delta(X)\le\Delta:=2pn=n/C^2$ and the $K_q$-extension property.

nodes.name: Sample spread random omni-absorber $A$
nodes.statement: Apply Theorem~\ref{thm:OmniSpread} to $X$ to get a distribution on omni-absorbers $A$ with $\Delta(A)\le C\Delta$ and spreadness $\Prob{\bigcup_L\{\mathcal{S}\subseteq\mathcal{Q}_A(L)\}}\le(n^{-(q-6)/2-2\beta})^{|\mathcal{S}|}$.

nodes.name: Regularity boost $J_A=G-(X\cup A)$
nodes.statement: For each $A\in\mathcal{A}$, apply Lemma~\ref{lem:RegBoost} to $J_A$ to obtain a near-$\frac{1}{2}\binom{n-2}{q-2}$-regular subhypergraph $\mathcal{D}_1^A\subseteq\mathrm{Design}(J_A,K_q)$.

nodes.name: Build bipartite design $\mathcal{D}_2^A$
nodes.statement: Define $\binom{q}{2}$-uniform $\mathcal{D}_2^A$ on $V(\mathcal{D}_2^A)=E(J_A)\cup X$ with edges $\{S:|S\cap E(J_A)|=1,\ G[S]\cong K_q\}$. Verify codegree, degree, and bipartiteness conditions.

nodes.name: Apply spread nibble to $\mathcal{D}^A$
nodes.statement: Apply Theorem~\ref{thm:spread-nibble} with parameters $r=\binom{q}{2}$, $\gamma=1/q$, $\beta=\min\{1/(2q-5),1/4\}$, $\alpha=8q^2\beta$ to get a spread distribution on $E(J_A)$-perfect matchings $M_A$, equivalently $K_q$-packings $\mathcal{M}_A$ of $G-A$ covering $J_A$ with $\ProbCond{\mathcal{S}\subseteq\mathcal{M}_A}{A=A'}\le(n^{-(q-3)})^{|\mathcal{S}|}$.

nodes.name: Combine into a $K_q$-decomposition
nodes.statement: Set $L_{A,M_A}:=X\setminus\bigcup M_A$ and pick $\mathcal{M}_A\cup\mathcal{Q}_A(L_{A,M_A})$, a $K_q$-decomposition of $K_n$.

nodes.name: Bound joint spread by partitioning $\mathcal{S}$
nodes.statement: For a $K_q$-packing $\mathcal{S}$, write $\Prob{\mathcal{S}\subseteq\mathcal{M}_A\cup\mathcal{Q}_A(L_{A,M_A})}\le\sum_{\mathcal{S}'\subseteq\mathcal{S}}\ProbCond{\mathcal{S}'\subseteq\mathcal{M}_A}{\bigcup_L\{\mathcal{S}\setminus\mathcal{S}'\subseteq\mathcal{Q}_A(L)\}}\Prob{\bigcup_L\{\mathcal{S}\setminus\mathcal{S}'\subseteq\mathcal{Q}_A(L)\}}$.

nodes.name: Plug in nibble and omni-absorber spreadness
nodes.statement: Apply (6.2) and (6.1) to bound conditional probabilities by $(1/n^{q-3})^{|\mathcal{S}'|}$ and $(1/n^{(q-6)/2+2\beta})^{|\mathcal{S}|-|\mathcal{S}'|}$ respectively. Since $q-3\ge(q-6)/2+2\beta$, sum over $\mathcal{S}'$ yields $\Prob{\mathcal{S}\subseteq\mathcal{M}_A\cup\mathcal{Q}_A(L_{A,M_A})}\le(1/n^{(q-6)/2+\beta})^{|\mathcal{S}|}$.

nodes.name: Theorem 1.3 implies Theorem 1.2 via Park-Pham
nodes.statement: Theorem~\ref{thm:spread-decomposition} together with the Park-Pham Theorem yields Theorem~\ref{thm:ExistenceSpread}; in fact the slightly stronger bound $p\geq n^{-(q-6)/2-\beta}$.

nodes.name: Booster density lower bound
nodes.statement: Every non-isolated vertex of a $K_q$-booster is in at least two cliques of each decomposition; double-counting yields rooted density $\ge 2/q$, so new techniques would be needed to prove Conjecture~\ref{conj:KKKMO} for general $q$.

nodes.name: Algorithmic vs non-constructive trade-off
nodes.statement: Direct embedding of both booster decompositions in $\mathcal{G}^{(q)}(n,p)$ would yield a randomized polynomial-time algorithm at the cost of an extra factor of $2$ in the threshold exponent ($p\ge n^{-(q-6)/4}$ vs $n^{-(q-6)/2}$-spread); using Park-Pham mitigates this at the cost of being non-constructive.
